Seasonally Decoupled Recovery of Flooded Cropland After the 2022 Sindh Floods: A Matched-Counterfactual Satellite Assessment
nodes.abstract: Flooded cropland in Sindh had not returned to its counterfactual vegetation condition four years after the 2022 floods, and the shortfall sits almost entirely in the summer (Kharif) season. We built 555,309 300-m cropland cells across 22 districts and tracked monthly Sentinel-2 normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI) and enhanced vegetation index (EVI) from January 2021 to September 2026. Cells with three or more Sentinel-1 water detections during August to October 2022 were treated as flooded and matched one-to-one with non-flooded cells on terrain, drainage proximity, cropland fraction, and pre-flood vegetation level and trend, giving 87,447 pairs with all seven covariates balanced (absolute standardized mean difference below 0.03). An event-study difference-in-differences model shows no pre-flood divergence (k = −1 coefficient +0.003, p = 0.43). Flooded cells fell 0.20 NDVI below controls in Kharif 2022, recovered to −0.06 by Rabi (winter) 2023–24, settled at about −0.11 through Kharif 2026. The result survives a placebo shock, three calipers, leave-one-district-out estimation, and a monotonic dose-response across flood-duration terciles (−0.13, −0.19, −0.28). Integrated Kharif NDVI in flooded cells stayed 0.30 to 0.60 units below controls in every summer from 2023 to 2026, whereas integrated Rabi NDVI exceeded controls from the second winter onward (flood duration × Kharif interaction, γ = −0.32, p = 4.4 × 10−10). Flood duration and post-flood standing-water persistence were the strongest predictors of time to recovery across mixed-effects, spatial, and gradient-boosted models. Trajectory clustering places 17% of matched cells in a persistent-deficit archetype; Larkana and Dadu hold 36% of them.

nodes.name: SWOT-Based 3D Mapping of an Ice-Dammed Lake Outburst Flood: A Case Study of Merzbacher Lake
nodes.abstract: Abstract Glacial lake outburst floods (GLOFs) are among the most destructive hazards in high-mountain regions and are expected to become increasingly important under ongoing glacier retreat and climate warming. However, quantifying the magnitude of individual GLOFs remains challenging because satellite observations typically capture changes in lake area but lack direct measurements of water-level drawdown, leading to large uncertainties in released-water estimates. Here, we develop a satellite-based framework that integrates Sentinel-2 imagery and Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) observations to reconstruct the three-dimensional evolution of an ice-dammed lake outburst flood. Using the July 2025 drainage of Merzbacher Lake in the central Tian Shan as a case study, we combine optical observations of lake-area collapse with SWOT-derived water-surface elevation changes to quantify event-scale water loss. Sentinel-2 observations show that the lake area decreased from 1.560 to 0.008 km², while SWOT measurements reveal a concurrent water-level decline from 3270.38 to 3257.83 m, corresponding to a drawdown of 12.55 m. Integrating these horizontal and vertical constraints yields an estimated drained-water volume of (9.84 ± 2.4) × 10⁶ m³. Residual water bodies concentrated near the glacier-contact outlet indicate an inferred outlet-control sector governing drainage. Our results demonstrate that SWOT enables GLOF assessment to move beyond two-dimensional lake-change detection toward quantitative stage–area–volume reconstruction. This approach provides a practical framework for estimating flood magnitude in remote glacierized regions where field observations are unavailable and offers new opportunities for satellite-based assessment of cryosphere-related hazards under a warming climate.

nodes.name: SDFNet: Snow Depth Retrieval Based on a Multi-Scale Feature Fusion Network for the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau
nodes.venue: Remote Sensing
nodes.abstract: High-resolution snow depth (SD) information supports hydrological and cryospheric studies in complex mountain regions. Coarse SD products limit representation of terrain-related snow variability in these environments. This study proposes SDFNet, a Snow Depth Fusion Network combining Sentinel-1 SAR, Landsat optical data, digital elevation model (DEM) variables, and fractional snow cover (FSC). Multi-scale feature extraction, channel enhancement, and feature aggregation modules represent relationships among these inputs. Observations from 95 meteorological stations across the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau supplied supervision and reference measurements for evaluation. Station SD was the regression target rather than a prediction input. In the station-based comparison, SDFNet achieved an RMSE of 5.246 cm and an R2 of 0.702. It had the lowest RMSE and highest R2 among the compared models. However, SD above 40 cm produced an RMSE of 21.927 cm and a bias of −16.061 cm, indicating substantial deep-snow underestimation. Sparse station coverage limits inference beyond the sampled environments, and independent spatial validation remains necessary.

nodes.name: Remote supervised exercise- and physical activity-based rehabilitation for post-stroke depression, anxiety, and quality of life: a systematic review, evidence map, and exploratory quantitative synthesis
nodes.venue: Frontiers in Psychiatry
nodes.abstract: Background Depression, anxiety, and reduced quality of life are common after stroke and may interfere with rehabilitation engagement and long-term recovery. Remote supervision can support home-based exercise or physical activity, but the available programs are complex packages that may also include coaching, caregiver involvement, education, and psychological support. We aimed to synthesize randomized evidence on depression, anxiety, and quality of life after remotely supervised exercise- or physical activity-based stroke rehabilitation, accounting for comparator type and co-interventions. Methods This systematic review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261394314) and reported according to PRISMA 2020. PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, SPORTDiscus, Cochrane Library, Embase, and Scopus were searched from inception to 1 March 2026. Randomized studies of remotely supervised exercise- or physical activity-based rehabilitation after ischemic or hemorrhagic stroke were eligible if depression, anxiety, or quality-of-life outcomes were extractable. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2, certainty was evaluated using GRADE, and a co-intervention sensitivity analysis examined the evidence remaining after exclusion of interventions with explicit psychological support. Results Six randomized studies involving 483 participants were included. Interventions, comparators, outcome instruments, and study designs were heterogeneous, precluding a primary pooled meta-analysis. The only directly analyzable depression effect against standard care came from Sun et al., a 12-week multidisciplinary telerehabilitation program that included online psychological counseling; the aligned Hedges g was 0.93 (95% CI 0.64 to 1.22), conventionally large, but certainty was very low. After this trial was excluded, no directly analyzable depression effect against standard care remained. Active-vs-active depression or distress findings did not establish superiority. Quality-of-life signals varied across instruments and comparators; no separable patient anxiety effect was available. Conclusion The included evidence concerns complex remote rehabilitation packages rather than exercise alone. A possible depression benefit is supported principally by one trial with a psychological-support co-intervention and is therefore fragile. Remote programs should not be regarded as stand-alone treatments for post-stroke depression or anxiety. Confirmatory trials should recruit or stratify participants by baseline psychiatric symptoms, prespecify psychiatric outcomes, and separate exercise from psychological and implementation components. Systematic review registration https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261394314 , identifier CRD420261394314.

nodes.name: Recent advances in artificial intelligence-driven hyperspectral imaging for tea quality evaluation and component detection
nodes.venue: Fourth International Conference on Optical Communication and Optical Information Processing (OCOIP 2026)
nodes.abstract: The integration of hyperspectral imaging (HSI) and artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a promising approach for rapid and nondestructive tea quality assessment. This review summarizes recent advances in AI-assisted HSI technologies for tea component quantification, quality grading, origin traceability, disease detection, and adulteration identification. The fundamental principles of HSI systems and commonly used machine learning and deep learning algorithms are first introduced. Subsequently, representative studies on tea physicochemical component prediction and quality evaluation are systematically analyzed. The advantages and limitations of conventional machine learning methods (PLSR, SVM, RF) and deep learning models (CNN, ResNet, GRU, transfer learning) are comparatively discussed. Furthermore, current challenges including limited model generalization, small-sample learning, high equipment costs, and insufficient standardization are critically reviewed. Finally, future research directions are proposed, including lightweight deep learning, multimodal data fusion, explainable artificial intelligence, and large-scale tea spectral databases. This review provides a comprehensive reference for promoting the industrial application of intelligent tea quality evaluation systems.

Predicted visual attention and cognitive demand in luxury beauty retail: an exploratory AI-based neuromarketing study
nodes.venue: Frontiers in Communication
nodes.abstract: Introduction This exploratory study examines how AI-supported neuromarketing tools can be used to predict visual attention and cognitive demand in a luxury beauty retail environment. Methods The research was conducted in a high-end cosmetics store in Zagreb, where 11 static images, selected from 21 photographs of the store, and a 9-minute in-store video recording, edited into an 85-second simulation of the consumer journey, were analyzed using a predictive platform informed by large-scale eye tracking and EEG datasets (eye-tracking data from approximately 180,000 participants and EEG data from 27,000 participants; more than 100 billion data points in total). No shoppers were tested; all reported values are model predictions. The analysis focused on how store layout, product positioning, visual hierarchy, and branded communication elements influence predicted focus, attentional efficiency, and cognitive effort. Results The results reveal several consistent patterns. Brand areas that were visually separated from competing stimuli attracted stronger, more sustained predicted attention, whereas visually crowded or externally exposed zones reduced attentional efficiency. Central product placement proved particularly effective when surrounded by fewer distracting elements, suggesting that spatial clarity can support more efficient visual processing of branded and product-related stimuli. At the AOI level, Engagement and Cognitive Demand rose together ( r = 0.90). In the video simulation, Cognitive Demand remained uniformly high while Focus varied with the field of view, and the two were not related. Discussion These findings highlight the interaction between attention allocation, cognitive load, visibility conditions, and spatial organization in luxury retail communication. Overall, the study demonstrates the value of AI-supported neuromarketing for understanding how consumers process visually complex retail spaces. It contributes to communication and consumer research by clarifying how visual structure and cognitive demand shape brand visibility and decision-related processing in luxury beauty retail. The findings also offer practical guidance for improving store design, in-store communication, and experiential branding strategies by applying state-of-the-art technology for predicting consumer behavior in visually complex retail environments.

nodes.name: Optimising Irish Fen Habitat Mapping: An Evaluation of Temporal Windowing and Spectral Features Using Google Earth Engine and Random Forest
nodes.venue: Sensors
nodes.abstract: High spectral similarity and overlapping habitat boundaries present a substantial challenge for mapping and monitoring Ireland’s ecologically vital fen ecosystems. This study establishes a reproducible remote sensing workflow by combining Google Earth Engine (GEE) with Sentinel-2 imagery for Irish fen classification. This study uses a Random Forest machine learning model to evaluate five temporal windows against three spectral feature sets across three distinct sites. The results indicate that a growing season window (June–September) incorporating both bands and spectral indices captures peak phenological information more effectively than annual composites, producing high within-site, pixel-level overall accuracy across all study sites (Scragh Bog: 95.24%, Liskeenan Fen: 94.13%, Ballymore Fen: 94.43%). Although raw spectral bands achieved marginally higher localised accuracies at Liskeenan (+0.24%) and Ballymore (+1.65%), the combined feature set was maintained as the standard workflow to ensure cross-site stability, biophysical parameterisation, and resilience against localised soil background noise. To accommodate narrow, fragmented geometries, training data was extracted via pixel-level stratified sampling; while this introduces spatial autocorrelation, classification outputs showed coherent within-site spatial patterns, although accuracy estimates remain subject to spatial autocorrelation. Crucially, the Google Earth Engine-based Random Forest model maintained stable within-site classification performance when reducing the training-testing ratio from a standard 80:20 split down to a highly constrained 50:50 split. Ultimately, this workflow provides a cloud-based framework for monitoring vulnerable wetland ecosystems under real-world geometric and ground-truth data limitations.

nodes.name: Multimodal Sensing and Machine Learning for Nondestructive Quality and Safety Assessment of Agricultural Products
nodes.venue: Chemosensors
nodes.abstract: The demand for non-destructive evaluation of agricultural products has stimulated the emergence of multimodal sensing technologies capable of integrating diverse quality- and safety-related information. Recent advances in multimodal sensing and machine learning (ML) have enabled intelligent platforms capable of integrating diverse physicochemical, structural, and biochemical information for comprehensive product characterization. This review summarizes the principles, data-processing strategies, and applications of multimodal sensing systems combining machine vision, visible-near-infrared spectroscopy, hyperspectral imaging, Raman and fluorescence techniques, electronic noses, and auxiliary information with ML algorithms. The complementary capabilities of different sensing modalities for evaluating external appearance, internal quality, chemical composition, freshness, spoilage, and safety hazards are discussed. Meanwhile, the roles of conventional ML and deep learning in feature extraction, pattern recognition, and multimodal data fusion are highlighted. Although advanced algorithms and increased data dimensions improve analytical performance, reliable deployment requires robust datasets, effective calibration transfer, model interpretability, uncertainty assessment, and independent validation. Future advances should prioritize self-supervised and few-shot learning, domain adaptation, physics-informed models, lightweight edge intelligence, and standardized benchmarking to improve model reliability, transferability, and scalability. These innovations will facilitate the deployment of intelligent sensing systems from laboratory environments to real-world agricultural quality and safety management.

nodes.name: Multimodal Joint Frequency Regulation Control for Thermal Power–Hybrid Energy Storage Systems Under AGC Time-Sharing Assessment
nodes.venue: Processes
nodes.abstract: In thermal power (TP) units equipped with hybrid energy storage (ES) systems, automatic generation control (AGC) command allocation and storage power control directly affect frequency regulation performance, assessment results, and operational sustainability. Existing strategies usually do not distinguish between AGC assessment periods and non-assessment periods. Therefore, ES devices may still charge or discharge when their output no longer contributes to the AGC assessment, resulting in unnecessary energy loss, reduced ramping capability, and poor state-of-charge (SOC) recovery. In addition, the available reserve capacity of TP units and the residual capacity of different storage devices are not fully utilized. To solve these problems, this paper proposes a joint frequency regulation control strategy for a thermal-hybrid ES system considering AGC time-sharing assessment characteristics and multimodal coordination. First, the AGC assessment process is analyzed according to the requirements of regulation rate, regulation time, and regulation accuracy. The response process of the thermal-hybrid ES system is divided into the initial response stage, acceleration stage, steady regulation stage, and assessment-ending stage. For upward and downward AGC command changes, an assessment-oriented optimal response trajectory is established. Based on the real-time output of the thermal unit, the overall frequency regulation reference command of the hybrid ES system is obtained. Second, a multimodal coordinated control strategy is developed. During the ramping stage, the operating mode is determined according to the SOC states of the battery and flywheel ES systems. The regulation command is allocated between the two devices according to their SOC margins, power characteristics, and charging or discharging constraints. Smooth correction factors are introduced to reduce excessive battery charging and discharging, while a nonlinear correction is used to prevent the flywheel from frequently operating outside its safe SOC range. During the non-assessment stage, a SOC recovery strategy is further designed by using the reserve capacity of the thermal unit and the remaining capacity of the storage devices. A case study is conducted using typical monthly AGC command data and actual response power data from a TP plant in Hubei Province. The rated capacities of the battery and flywheel are set to 2.0 MWh and 0.2 MWh, respectively. Compared with single-storage, full-compensation, proportional allocation, and partial multimodal control schemes, the proposed strategy achieves the best overall performance. The average regulation rate index, regulation time index, regulation accuracy index, comprehensive evaluation index, and AGC assessment success rate reach 1.99, 0.99, 0.99, 1.91, and 99%, respectively. The proposed strategy also obtains the highest net benefit of 12.023 million yuan.

nodes.name: MSFANet: a multi-scale feature aggregation network for tobacco pest recognition
nodes.venue: Frontiers in Plant Science
nodes.abstract: Introduction Tobacco is a globally significant economic crop, and pest infestation represents one of the primary factors contributing to declines in both yield and quality. However, tobacco pests encompass a wide variety of species that differ substantially in morphology and scale. Field-captured images are frequently subject to complex background interference and class imbalance, presenting considerable challenges for automated recognition. Existing deep learning approaches remain limited in their capacity for multi-scale feature extraction and discriminative feature representation under such conditions. To address these challenges, this study proposes a Multi-Scale Feature Aggregation Network (MSFANet) for tobacco pest recognition, formulated here as a single-label image classification task. Methods To address scale variation and complex field backgrounds, two task-oriented modules were developed. The Multi-Scale Pyramid Pooling (MSPP) module aggregates contextual information across multiple receptive fields through parallel feature extraction and adaptive cross-branch fusion. The Hierarchical Feature Fusion Block (HFFB) subsequently refines the feature representations through spatial gating and partial convolution. An auxiliary classification head and Focal Loss were incorporated during training to provide intermediate supervision and address class imbalance, respectively. Results The effectiveness of MSFANet was evaluated on a dataset comprising 13 tobacco-associated pest and natural-enemy categories. The model achieved accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score of 97.63%, 97.89%, 97.59%, and 97.71%, respectively, with a parameter count of 1.21 M. Among the models trained from random initialization, MSFANet shared the highest accuracy while using the fewest parameters. Discussion By combining multi-scale contextual aggregation with hierarchical feature refinement, MSFANet achieved accurate classification across the 13 tobacco-associated categories under complex field conditions. The proposed method provides effective technical support for automated and precision-oriented pest monitoring in tobacco fields, offering practical value for advancing precise pest management and the broader development of smart agriculture.

nodes.name: Long-Term Mangrove Dynamics and Environmental Associations in the Sundarbans, Bangladesh: Integrating Remote Sensing, Machine Learning, and Explainable AI
nodes.venue: Remote Sensing
nodes.abstract: Mangrove ecosystems are increasingly threatened by anthropogenic disturbances and climate change, despite providing ecological services, including biodiversity conservation, coastal protection, and blue carbon storage. Long-term evaluations of mangrove dynamics and associated environmental conditions remain limited, particularly in the Sundarbans, the largest mangrove forest in the world. This study examined the spatiotemporal dynamics of the Sundarbans mangrove ecosystem, Bangladesh, using multi-temporal Landsat imagery (1990–2025), Random Forest (RF), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). Model performance was evaluated using the Global Mangrove Watch (GMW) dataset and spatially blocked holdout validation. Classification accuracy was high (94.56–100%) under internal and spatially blocked validation (93.5–99.8%), whereas comparison with GMW yielded lower accuracies (66.4–95.7%). Change detection showed that mangrove area expanded from 2096.66 km2 in 1990 to 3875.95 km2 in 2025, a net gain of almost 1779.29 km2, with substantial inter-period variability and a pronounced mapped decline between 2000 and 2005. SHAP analysis indicated that the relative contributions of model predictors changed over time, with NDVI contributing more strongly to model predictions in recent years than NDWI and NDMI. Mangrove gain, loss, and net change were statistically associated with cyclone exposure and elevation, while precipitation and river discharge showed less consistent relationships. This study highlights a practical method for monitoring spectral dynamics in vulnerable coastal ecosystems and supports mangrove conservation.

nodes.name: Leveraging satellite products and machine learning/deep learning models for the upgrading of agro-advisory systems in India: A bibliometric and systematic narrative review
nodes.venue: Plant Science Today
nodes.abstract: A comprehensive bibliometric review was conducted to evaluate the most relevant literature retrieved from the Scopus database, resulting in the identification of 125 relevant publications from an initial pool of 1948 records through a screening process based on the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA). The bibliometric analysis revealed a significant increasing trend in year-wise publications and citations, wherein India and the US emerged as the leading contributors with total publications of 34 and 25 respectively. Notably, the systematic narrative review highlights that agro-advisory systems (AAS) have increased farmer income by 83 %, improved crop yields by 6–25 % and enhanced farm profitability by 15–26 % in India. Despite these achievements, conventional AAS frameworks that rely predominantly on automatic weather stations (AWS) continue to face critical limitations, including sparse spatial coverage, restricted agro-meteorological observations, data discontinuities and inadequate representation of local microclimatic variability. To address these limitations, the study highlights the importance of integrating AWS observations with high-resolution satellite products through downscaling and subsequent assimilation within the Weather Research and Forecasting Data Assimilation (WRFDA) framework to improve the spatial accuracy of weather forecasts and facilitate the delivery of reliable block-level and village-level agro-advisories. However, the operational implementation of satellite-assisted weather forecasting using the Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) model is often constrained by latency in data availability, as many high-resolution satellite products require several hours to multiple days for processing and dissemination. In order to overcome this limitation, the review further demonstrates the considerable potential of machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) models trained using historical satellite observations along with meteorological predictors derived from numerical weather prediction (NWP) systems for enhancing downscaling capabilities and improving forecast accuracy. The results inferred that the satellite-based weather forecasting using ML and DL architectures achieved strong predictive performance, with reported R² values of up to 0.982, 0.976 and 0.95 for rainfall, temperature and aerosol concentration respectively. These findings demonstrate the increasing potential of satellite-driven ML and DL approaches for high-resolution weather forecasting and their applicability to next-generation, location-specific agro-advisory services. However, their operational utilisation depends on the availability of adequate computational infrastructure, skilled human resources, economic feasibility, institutional coordination and farmer acceptance. Therefore, the future of satellite-based AAS lies in developing computationally efficient, economically viable and farmer centric decision support platforms capable of translating complex forecast information into timely, understandable and actionable recommendations for climate-resilient agriculture.

nodes.name: Label-Free Quantitative Evaluation of Land Cover Segmentation Models for Remote Sensing Imagery: A Context-Aware Model Based on OpenStreetMap and a Digital Surface Model
nodes.venue: Remote Sensing
nodes.abstract: Segmentation performance is measured against pixel-wise ground truth (GT); without it, that measurement cannot be made. Remote sensing segmentation models are evaluated likewise, yet operational systems receive new unlabeled images, and the properties of those images shift with season, region, and sensor aging. A way to check performance outside the training dataset is needed. We propose quantifying segmentation output without labels, using public geospatial data: a random-forest context-aware model predicts class area composition from OpenStreetMap (OSM) and digital surface model (DSM) statistics. Quantile mapping transforms its output to match the distribution of measured compositions, yielding the expected distribution, and the Label-Free Composition Score (LFCS) is the similarity between that distribution and the composition of the segmentation output. The context-aware model is fitted only to geospatial features and GT compositions from the segmentation model’s training dataset, so the expected distribution is independent of the segmentation model’s structure, parameters, and outputs while depending on that dataset’s GT, class scheme, and composition distribution. The evaluation stage requires no GT labels. To test the method, we saved 430 segmentation model checkpoints from 75 training runs under six controlled training variations, so that the mean intersection over union (mIoU) of each, measured against GT on validation tiles held out of training, was known in advance. These GT mIoU values ranged from 0.04 to 0.69. The models were grouped by GT mIoU in steps of 0.1. Their mean LFCS rose with every step: from 0.474 to 0.937 on held-out images from the same dataset, and from 0.467 to 0.893 on 900 globally distributed unlabeled images. Existing measures that read only a model’s own output tracked GT mIoU less consistently. Rebuilding the entire method reproduced the same behavior on two public datasets with different class schemes, confirming the validity of the method under the conditions tested.

nodes.name: Intraoperative Very High-Frequency Activity for Localization of the Epileptogenic Zone: An International Multicenter Study
nodes.abstract: Background and Objectives Interictal spikes on intraoperative electrocorticography have been used to localize the epileptogenic zone but have limited specificity. We hypothesized that identifying spatially distributed, spike-associated very high-frequency activity (vHFA; 500-2,000 Hz) would improve the ability of spikes to localize the epileptogenic zone. We aimed to characterize spike-associated vHFA and to determine whether a seizure outcome prediction model incorporating vHFA could be externally validated across independent centers. Methods This retrospective two-center cohort study included patients with drug-resistant focal epilepsy who underwent electrocorticography and subsequent resection between January 2016 and May 2025. Spikes occurring across contacts within 50 ms were classified as co-occurring; all others were classified as isolated. We determined whether vHFA was associated with co-occurring spikes. We then assessed whether contacts enriched in vHFA-positive co-occurring spikes were more likely to be located within the resected region among seizure-free patients. Finally, we determined whether the rate of such spikes remaining outside the resection predicted seizure outcomes across the two centers. Results Among 56 patients (mean age: 21.2 years; 26 females), we identified 132,359 spikes, of which 1,925 were vHFA-positive. The vHFA peak preceded the associated spike peak by 8.0 ms (95%CI: 5.0-16.0). vHFA-positive spikes were more likely to be classified as co-occurring, even after adjustment for anatomy and inter-electrode distance (OR: 3.43; 95%CI: 2.82-4.17). Among the 35 seizure-free patients, contacts with higher rates of vHFA-positive co-occurring spikes were more likely to be resected (OR: 11.92 per occurrence/min; 95%CI: 5.62-25.32). This association was stronger than that observed for all spikes (OR: 1.09 per occurrence/min; 95%CI: 1.06-1.11). Twenty patients experienced postoperative seizure recurrence; a higher proportion of vHFA-positive co-occurring spikes in preserved areas was associated with recurrence (OR: 3.22 per 0.01 increase in proportion; 95%CI: 1.14-9.12). In bidirectional cross-center validation, models incorporating vHFA-positive co-occurring spikes yielded areas under the receiver operating characteristic curves of 0.80 and 0.69, with better performance when the model was developed using the larger sample. Discussion Spike-associated vHFA may identify a biologically meaningful subset of interictal spikes involved in propagation across the epileptogenic zone. vHFA-positive co-occurring spikes may represent a generalizable intraoperative biomarker of the epileptogenic zone.

nodes.name: Integration of IoT And Satellite Data for Real-Time Agricultural Crop Stress Monitoring Using Spatio-Temporal Transformers
nodes.venue: Turkish Journal of Engineering
nodes.abstract: This research work presents an integrated framework for real-time crop stress monitoring that combines ground-based Internet of Things (IoT) sensors and multi-temporal satellite remote sensing data. Due to growing environmental uncertainty and limited resources, the early identification of crop stress is crucial for maximizing agricultural productivity. IoT sensors yield localized, real-time measurements of key variables like soil moisture, temperature, and humidity, whereas satellite images yield wide-area vegetation and thermal indicators (e.g., NDVI, EVI, LST). The solution utilizes a Spatio-Temporal Transformer (ST-Transformer) model to integrate these heterogeneous data streams to make early crop disease and irrigation stress detection. By integrating spatial satellite imagery with temporal IoT sequences, STT leverages attention mechanisms to offer a more holistic analysis, which translates to an impressive accuracy of 88% and a solid F1-Score of 0.855. This dual capacity to concurrently handle spatial and temporal dimensions allows STT to effectively generalize across diverse crop stress categories, providing insights that are both timely and actionable

nodes.name: Integrating Time Series, Remote Sensing and Computational Intelligence for Flood Prediction in a Data-Scarce Tropical Floodplain of the Lower Magdalena River Basin, Colombia
nodes.abstract: Abstract Flood prediction in environmentally vulnerable and data-constrained regions remains a major challenge, particularly in tropical floodplains where hydrometeorological variability, sparse monitoring networks, and uneven spatial coverage limit the reliability of conventional forecasting approaches. This study proposes a hybrid and modular framework for flood prediction in the lower Magdalena River basin, Colombia, integrating long-term rainfall and river-level time series from IDEAM stations with spatial contextual information from remote sensing products, digital elevation data, spatial interpolation, principal component analysis (PCA), and computational intelligence models. Point-based observations were transformed into continuous spatial fields using inverse distance weighting (IDW) and ordinary kriging, and PCA was subsequently applied to reduce dimensionality and improve training efficiency. Artificial neural networks (ANN) and support vector regression (SVR) were then used to reconstruct monthly predictive maps, which were evaluated against 2022 reference patterns using visual comparison and mean absolute percentage error (MAPE). The results show that predictive performance depended strongly on the interaction between the interpolation method, the learning model, and the target variable. The ordinary kriging–PCA–ANN configuration provided the most hydrologically coherent performance for water-level prediction, preserving regional continuity and the dominant spatial structure. In contrast, IDW-based configurations were more suitable for preserving local rainfall variability, although they also showed greater spatial error dispersion. A comparative synthesis of representative-month and annual MAPE evidence across the eight evaluated configurations confirmed that no single configuration was universally superior, reinforcing the need for variable-sensitive model selection. Overall, the proposed framework provides a reproducible and transferable basis for spatially explicit flood prediction in flood-prone and data-scarce environments, with clear relevance for environmental monitoring and future flood early-warning systems.

nodes.name: ICU Physical Environments Used for Family Conferences: A Multimodal Qualitative Evaluation with ICU Team Members
nodes.venue: Critical Care Medicine
nodes.abstract: Objectives: Family-clinician communication is central to high-quality care for critically ill patients. Although previous work has focused on improving how and what is communicated, little is known about where this high-stakes communication takes place and how it is shaped by the physical environment. Our objectives were to characterize ICU spaces typically used for family conferences and identify modifiable environmental features that influence communication. Design: We conducted a multimodal qualitative study of 17 spaces typically used for family conferences across four adult ICUs in a U.S. academic medical center. Healthcare design and architecture experts independently assessed architectural plans and photographs to characterize spatial features. Then, we conducted semi-structured interviews with 23 ICU team members (nurses, social workers, case managers) to elicit perspectives on and experiences within these spaces. We conducted qualitative content analysis using a combined inductive and deductive approach. Setting: A total of 17 family conference spaces across four adult ICUs in a U.S. academic medical center. Participants: A total of 23 ICU team members. Interventions: None. Results: The 17 analyzed spaces included designated family-communication rooms ( n = 2), multipurpose rooms ( n = 6), visitor lounges ( n = 4), and public areas ( n = 5; lobbies/hallways). Study participants preferred designated spaces, as they provide privacy, prevent interruption, and facilitate emotional support. Conversely, multipurpose and public areas are prone to distractions and interruptions from conflicting uses. We identified key environmental features that support communication: proximity to patients, flexible furniture layout, and nonclinical ambiance. Conclusions: Family conferences occur in a variety of physical environments in and around adult ICUs, ranging from intentionally designed rooms to elevator lobbies. ICU team members perceive that physical environments have an important influence on communication quality, and we identified pragmatic opportunities to improve existing spaces.

nodes.name: From Understanding to Action: A Survey on Closed-Loop Multimodal Agents
nodes.abstract: Abstract Multimodal systems are increasingly moving from understanding-centered models to agents that inspect observations, call tools, interact with digital or physical environments, and update behavior from feedback. Existing surveys have covered multimodal large language models, tool use, GUI and web agents, embodied agents, and agent evaluation, but these lines of work are often organized by capability, modality, task domain, or system architecture. This survey offers an evidence-centered account of closed-loop multimodal agency. We define evidence as an inspectable intermediate state that connects multimodal observation to downstream decision, action, or revision. Based on this definition, we organize 105 reviewed papers around five evidence operations: active perception, cognitive workspace, knowledge-tool expansion, environment control, and learning from feedback. We further introduce the O-P-G-C evaluation lens, which separates outcome, process, grounding, and cost-risk signals. This lens clarifies why task success alone is insufficient for evaluating multimodal agents: a system may complete a task while using weak evidence, following an invalid trajectory, or incurring unnecessary cost and risk. Our analysis shows that current benchmark protocols cover outcome most consistently, while grounding, cost-risk, and failure diagnosis remain less uniformly supported. We conclude by identifying future research directions in evidence trace reporting, generalization across inputs and environments, feedback learning without error amplification, and cost-risk-aware deployment.

nodes.name: Damage Criticality Assessment from Aerial Imagery Using a Heterogeneous CNN–Vision Transformer Ensemble: A UAV-Assisted Remote Sensing Approach for Post-Earthquake Emergency Response
nodes.venue: Applied Sciences
nodes.abstract: Advances in remote sensing and unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) technologies are enabling faster and more effective post-earthquake disaster assessment. Rapid identification of aerial images indicating critical damage is essential for directing emergency response teams to areas where urgent assistance, field inspection, and resource allocation are most needed. However, manually reviewing large volumes of heterogeneous aerial imagery is time-consuming and may delay emergency response operations. This study proposes a heterogeneous CNN–Vision Transformer Voting Ensemble (CTVE) for automated damage criticality assessment from high- and low-altitude aerial imagery. Eight CNN architectures and six vision transformer models are comparatively evaluated on four heterogeneous datasets that differ in altitude, viewing angle, scene characteristics, and damage appearance. Different ensemble combinations are evaluated across the datasets in terms of classification performance and computational time. Based on this evaluation, the selected CTVE combines ConvNeXtBase, DenseNet169, ResNet50, Xception, and DeiT through hard majority voting, achieving a mean accuracy of 94.82% and a mean macro F1-score of 91.44%, with equal weighting across datasets. These results support the effectiveness of the selected heterogeneous ensemble for damage criticality assessment under diverse aerial imaging conditions.

nodes.name: Cross-Resolution Fusion of AlphaEarth Foundations Embeddings and GF-1 Imagery via Semantic Anchor-Graph Enhancement for Litchi Orchard Extraction
nodes.venue: Remote Sensing
nodes.abstract: Litchi is an important cash crop in China. Accurate litchi orchard extraction is crucial for agricultural management and economic development. However, litchi orchards are spectrally very similar to evergreen broad-leaved forests and are poorly resolved in medium- and low-resolution satellite imagery, so large-scale extraction remains challenging. A cross-resolution fusion network via semantic anchor-graph enhancement (SAGE-Net) is therefore proposed, using a dual-branch encoder–decoder to aggregate complementary features of AlphaEarth Foundations (AEF) embeddings and GF-1 imagery. To enable semantic interaction across resolutions, the SAGE module is designed to gather the AEF embeddings into a few semantic anchors, reason over the anchor graph, and scatter them back under GF-1 guidance, so that semantic content and spatial extent are supplied by the source better suited to each. To refine the coarse prediction to full resolution without discarding what is already reliable, the reliability-adaptive correction (RAC) head is designed to gate a detail-guided correction by the confidence and local consistency of that prediction, concentrating refinement where it is uncertain. In Shenzhen, SAGE-Net attains the highest IoU (0.5660) and F1-score (0.7229) among eight comparison methods, with a Precision of 0.7162 and a Recall of 0.7297. Under stricter protocols that separate the training and the evaluation patches by a 256 m buffer or by whole spatial blocks, the IoU falls to 0.5224 and 0.5000 and SAGE-Net remains the most accurate of the networks retested, by a smaller margin. The results demonstrate the value of role-aware enhancement and reliability-adaptive correction for fine-grained orchard mapping, and confirm AEF embeddings as an effective supplementary data source for large-scale mapping.

nodes.name: Comparing Human Gaze and Vision–Language Model Saliency Predictions in Safety-Relevant Scenes
nodes.venue: Applied Sciences
nodes.abstract: Human visual attention plays an important role in how people perceive and respond to environments containing potential risks. It is unclear whether vision–language models (VLMs) can predict where people look in such scenes. This exploratory study compares human gaze with VLM saliency predictions in safety-relevant scenes. Ten participants freely viewed 33 scene images while their gaze was recorded with eye-tracking glasses. Four VLMs (GPT-4o, Gemini 2.5 Pro, Gemini 2.5 Flash and Claude Sonnet 4) were prompted to predict gaze points for the same images, and the resulting maps were compared with the human gaze maps using standard saliency metrics. All four models showed positive spatial agreement with human gaze on the standard metrics (mean Pearson correlation 0.53 for GPT-4o), but a simple centre baseline scored higher. After correcting for centre bias, three of the four models remained above chance. The results for GPT-4o were stable across repeated runs and did not depend on the instructions in the prompt. Overall, current VLMs can partly predict where people look in safety-relevant scenes from a prompt alone, without any eye-tracking training data, but their predictions remain limited.

nodes.name: Classification and Remote Sensing Characterization of Large Catastrophic Landslides in the Southeastern Tibetan Plateau, China
nodes.venue: Remote Sensing
nodes.abstract: Large catastrophic landslides in the southeastern Tibetan Plateau are characterized by huge volumes and complex chains that frequently cause river damming and casualties. Based on field surveys, multi-temporal satellite imagery, Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV), Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) deformation measurements, and meteorological and seismic records, this study classifies these landslides into three types by their initiation and disaster-chain processes: (1) rock–ice avalanche → debris flow → landslide dam; (2) debris flow → landslide dam; (3) rock avalanche → landslide dam. Representative cases illustrate the material sources, initiation settings, and downstream impacts of each type. The occurrence of such landslides is influenced by the interplay of four groups of factors: fractured rock masses and abundant loose deposits provide the material basis; high mountains and narrow river valleys provide the spatial framework for landslide evolution and promote river blockage; pronounced climatic changes provide the background conditions and may affect slope stability in glaciated areas through glacier retreat; and frequent strong earthquakes can both instantaneously trigger failure and cause cumulative damage that predisposes slopes to subsequent failures. Ongoing climate warming and repeated seismic activity are expected to increase landslide susceptibility, highlighting the urgency of multi-hazard early warning and proactive mitigation. This study supports early warning prioritization and risk governance in high-mountain valleys across the Tibetan Plateau.

nodes.name: CFUNet: An Adaptive RGB–Depth Cross-Modal Fusion Network for Pavement Crack Segmentation
nodes.abstract: Abstract Accurate pavement crack segmentation is essential for intelligent road inspection and preventive pavement maintenance. However, existing RGB-based semantic segmentation methods are highly sensitive to illumination variations, while conventional RGB–Depth fusion strategies often fail to effectively exploit complementary appearance and geometric information. To address these limitations, this paper proposes CFUNet, a novel dual-branch RGB–Depth semantic segmentation framework based on a mid-level fusion strategy. The proposed network adopts two independent ResNet50 encoders to extract modality-specific features from RGB images and depth maps. An Enhanced Weighted Fusion (EWF) module is introduced to perform adaptive cross-modal feature aggregation, while a Lightweight Fusion Vision Transformer (LFVit) enhances global semantic representation with reduced computational complexity. Furthermore, a Frequency-aware Upsampling (FAUpSample) module is designed to preserve high-frequency boundary information during decoder reconstruction. Extensive experiments on a public RGB–Depth pavement crack dataset demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms representative CNN-based, Transformer-based, and multi-modal segmentation networks in terms of Precision, Recall, F1-score, and Intersection over Union (IoU). Ablation studies further verify the effectiveness of each proposed module and demonstrate that their collaborative optimization substantially improves segmentation performance. The proposed CFUNet provides an accurate and computationally efficient solution for intelligent pavement crack segmentation and shows considerable potential for deployment in practical road inspection systems.

nodes.name: CAP-DBNet: A Class-Adaptive Prototype-Guided Dual-Branch Collaborative Network for Remote Sensing Image Semantic Segmentation
nodes.venue: Remote Sensing
nodes.abstract: High-resolution remote sensing image semantic segmentation faces challenges from large-scale variation, fine boundary preservation, and class imbalance. This paper proposes CAP-DBNet, a compact framework that combines a RepViT M2.3 backbone with a global–local collaborative decoder (GLCD), a class-adaptive hybrid loss (CAHL), and a class-adaptive prototype-guided calibration module (CAPC). CAP-DBNet integrates class-center global and window-local modeling through bidirectional feature exchange, mini-batch class-frequency-aware supervision, and prototype-based residual calibration. Rather than introducing an isolated new attention or prototype mechanism, this work focuses on the coordinated design of these components within an efficient segmentation framework. In five repeated experiments with different random seeds, CAP-DBNet achieves average mIoUs of 85.16%, 88.32%, and 55.75% on Vaihingen, Potsdam, and LoveDA, respectively, improving over the same-backbone LOGCAN++ baseline by 1.43, 1.24, and 1.44 percentage points. Compared with D2LS under our evaluation protocol, CAP-DBNet uses 3.55× fewer parameters and requires 8.35× fewer floating-point operations (FLOPs). These results demonstrate an accuracy-efficiency-oriented global–local and class-adaptive framework for remote sensing semantic segmentation across three public benchmarks.

nodes.name: BTSR-Net: Boundary–topology guided structural refinement for high-resolution remote sensing image segmentation
nodes.venue: PLOS One
nodes.abstract: Semantic segmentation of high-resolution remote sensing imagery in complex urban scenes often suffers from insufficient modeling of boundary neighborhoods, causing ambiguity near class interfaces and weakening the continuity of elongated structures. To address this issue, we propose a Boundary-Topology-Guided Structural Refinement Network (BTSR-Net). Built upon HRNet-OCR, BTSR-Net introduces a Geometric Boundary–Distance Branch (GBD) with joint boundary–distance supervision to capture spatial transitions around class boundaries, a Multi-scale Topology-Guided Structural Fusion (MTSF) module to enhance connectivity representation of elongated structures, and a dual-stream structural refinement mechanism to perform local residual correction within a boundary-distance-defined refinement narrow-band. Experiments on the ISPRS Potsdam and Vaihingen datasets demonstrate improvements in overall segmentation accuracy, boundary quality, and structural connectivity. On Potsdam, BTSR-Net achieves 84.70% mIoU, 43.17% mBIoU, and 81.63% clDice, exceeding the baseline by 2.91, 5.66, and 3.74 percentage points, respectively. On Vaihingen, it achieves 93.94% mIoU, 73.90% mBIoU, and 95.46% clDice, with corresponding improvements of 2.27, 9.39, and 2.12 percentage points. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of BTSR-Net for structure-sensitive semantic segmentation in high-resolution remote sensing imagery.

nodes.name: Artificial Intelligence for Engineering-Grade Parametric CAD: A Critical Review of Representations, Large Language Models, and Agentic Design Systems
nodes.venue: Machines
nodes.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly expanding computer-aided design (CAD) from shape generation toward generative, conversational, and agentic engineering. However, most AI–CAD evaluations remain dominated by geometric similarity and execution success, while industrial CAD depends on editable parameters, design intent, stable feature histories, manufacturing constraints, and downstream CAD/CAE reuse. This structured critical review synthesizes 107 sources, principally from 2020–2026, across constrained sketches, boundary representations (B-Reps), parametric sequences, executable CAD programs, large language and multimodal models, CAD agents, commercial-CAD integration, and CAD–CAE. Rather than organizing the field only by model family, the review compares methods through the engineering information preserved and the behavior of generated models after modification. The synthesis identifies a consistent evidence gap: geometric validity and program execution are increasingly strong, whereas native feature-tree robustness, persistent references, design-intent preservation, and downstream verification remain weakly benchmarked. To address this gap, we propose the engineering-grade AI–CAD (EG–CAD) framework, in which geometric validity and executability are mandatory gates followed by parametric editability, constraint/design-intent preservation, feature-history robustness, engineering compliance, and downstream usability. A reference agent architecture and staged roadmap connect these criteria to CAD/CAM/CAE and smart-manufacturing workflows, reframing AI–CAD as an engineering automation problem rather than a shape-generation task.

nodes.name: Accurate Extraction of Phenotypic Parameters for DUS Testing of Oudemansiella raphanipes Based on Deep Learning
nodes.venue: Journal of Fungi
nodes.abstract: To enable the rapid and accurate acquisition of phenotypic parameters during distinctness, uniformity, and stability (DUS) testing of edible mushroom varieties, and to address the low efficiency, strong subjectivity, and insufficient standardization of conventional manual measurement methods, this study used the fruiting bodies of Oudemansiella raphanipes as the research object and proposed an automatic phenotypic parameter extraction method based on deep learning instance segmentation. An instance-segmentation dataset containing 473 O. raphanipes images and 1419 annotated objects was constructed, and the YOLOv11s-seg model was improved by introducing the lightweight feature-extraction network StarNet_s050 to construct the YOLOv11s-star-seg model, thereby improving model inference efficiency and meeting practical application requirements. Under standardized imaging conditions, pileus and stipe regions were obtained from the instance-segmentation results, and image-scale calibration was combined to automatically extract DUS phenotypic parameters, including pileus diameter, pileus context thickness, stipe length, and stipe diameter, while quantitatively describing stipe shape. The experimental results showed that the YOLOv11s-star-seg model performed well in the instance segmentation of O. raphanipes, achieving an mAP50 of 99.1%, an F1 value of 98.9%, and an mIoU of 97.86%; compared with the YOLOv11s-seg model, the number of parameters was reduced by 39% and the inference time was reduced by 27%, thereby achieving model lightweighting while maintaining high segmentation accuracy. The automatically extracted results showed high consistency with the manual measurements; the coefficients of determination (R2) from linear regression fitting for stipe length, stipe diameter, and pileus diameter all exceeded 0.96, indicating that the method can effectively replace part of the manual measurement process. The results can provide technical support for the digitalization of DUS testing of O. raphanipes, intelligent breeding of edible mushrooms, and accurate phenotypic identification.
